To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
SDG in fl axseed is present in a polymer, which consists of SDG and 3-hydroxyl-3-methyl-glutaric acid residues.
the SDG content is high in Swedish and Danish flaxseed and that SDG is linked to a strait chain, oligomeric, non-phenolic “polymer”.

(i) the HPLC method developed is a reliable and sensitive method for quantification and analysis of SDG and other glucosides in flaxseed; and (ii) a strait chain polymer with an average composition consisting of 5 SDG residues inter-linked with 4 3-hydroxyl-3-methylglutaric acid residues is present in flaxseed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a quantitative method for the determination of SDG and the structure elucidation of the “flaxseed phenolic polymer”.
the identification and quantification of phenolic compounds in flaxonseed.
the identification and quantification of SDGCs in flaxseed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
SDG in flaxonseed is present in an oligomeric structure.
the flaxseed “polymer” consists of a strait chain of SDG units interlinked with 3-hydroxyl-3-methylglutaric acid units.

the flaxseed “polymer” is a strait chain polymeric compound with an average composition consisting of five SDG molecules and four 3-hydryxy-3-methyglutaric acid (HMG) molecules interlinked with a β-D-glucopyrannose residue.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SDG content is a characteristic of the cultivar, that the SDG is linked in a strait chain polymer, and that the SDG concentration is higher in the defatted flour compared with the seed.
the flaxseed “polymer” is an oligomeric lignan-glucarate with an average composition and a strait chain structure.
we developed a method for quantitative analysis of SDG, which was applied to 29 cultivars.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the SDG content of flaxseed can be determined in a reliable way by the HPLC method developed.
SDG is a valuable component of flaxseed and can be quantified in flaxseed extracts by the developed method.
the flaxseed lignans are bound in an oligomeric structure and that this polymer can be quantitatively released by base hydrolysis.
